status: source checkpoint and owned SQL controls; integrated Rust verification owned by orchestrator
scope: Client lifecycle mutations take tenant publication writer before client rows or application advisory locks and retain it through the same transaction commit.

owned_postgresql.isolation: Separate disposable tmpfs PostgreSQL container; no shared database or instance mutation.

controls.name: writer waits before client row
controls.method: Connection A holds tenant FOR SHARE. Connection B obtains the same tenant FOR NO KEY UPDATE before updating a client with an enabled Kubernetes online profile. pg_stat_activity confirms B waits on a lock.

controls.name: publication client read remains available
controls.method: While B waits, A reads the client FOR SHARE under a one-second statement timeout and sees active.

controls.name: writer commits and preserves lifecycle invalidation
controls.method: After A commits, B commits disabled client status and the actual online-profile AFTER trigger sets enabled=false.

owned_postgresql.cleanup: All control rows removed, then owned container and private metadata removed.

ci_regression.name: client_lifecycle_writer_waits_before_client_row_and_preserves_invalidation
ci_regression.coverage: Actual PgClientRepository.upsert and PgPolicies.signing_fence with a real enabled online profile; client read must not block while writer waits at tenant admission.

limitations: The SQL control executes the production lock SQL and actual database triggers, not compiled repository methods or cryptographic issuance.
No worker Cargo, nextest, ignored integration tests or full suite were executed; composed verification belongs to the orchestrator.
This bug fix does not approve or activate proposed outbound SCIM, device or Kubernetes online protocols.
metadata: No SQLx query macro text or bind changes.
